errors.text: The hypothesis predicts a single-phase BCC product, whereas the target result is a mixed structure of approximately 83% FCC and 17% BCC.

It treats an FCC-to-BCC transformation as the central strengthening mechanism, although the target attributes strengthening primarily to nanocrystalline grain boundaries, milling-induced dislocations, solid-solution strengthening, and retention of a mixed FCC/BCC structure.
The proposed ~1050°C HCP-precipitation threshold is not established by the cited evidence; the evidence concerns materially different HEA systems and cannot validate this boundary for CoCrFeNiTi.

The third falsification criterion is logically inconsistent: increased HCP content and reduced hardness at 1100°C would support the proposed upper-temperature boundary rather than falsify the hypothesis.
